_doc: Fixtures still routed OUT of the in-process differential oracle because their spend needs a cryptographic witness that the plain oracle cannot synthesise from bare args. Post-mortem remediation #1 gave the oracle REAL secp256k1: every stateless/stateful ECDSA-checkSig / checkMultiSig fixture that could be given a real signature was MOVED to conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/ (executed for real on @bsv/sdk Spend) and removed from this list. What REMAINS here is genuinely out of reach for the current TS real-crypto harness: (a) EC point / hash-preimage / Rabin / post-quantum (SLH-DSA, WOTS+) primitives whose witnesses are not a plain secp256k1 signature and are still covered by the Go conformance/script_execution_test.go real-crypto path + per-family codegen goldens; (b) Go-only proof-system fixtures (compilers:[go]) with no TS codegen; (c) one SDK corner case (all-readonly-cleanstack). Each entry names the blocker. See conformance/witnesses/README.md.

exempt.reason: zero-mutable-field StatefulSmartContract (issue #44): RunarContract.prepareCall derives isStateful from stateFields.length>0, which is false here, so it exposes the auto-injected SigHashPreimage as a REQUIRED user arg and the standard call([null]) continuation path does not apply — the tx-context preimage cannot be supplied via the SDK call() harness. FOLLOW-UP: drive it via a hand-built preimage. Still covered by the Go tx-context path.
